01.i2v_prompt: A robotic arm opens the door of a wooden box. The video stops immediately after the wooden box's door is opened. Maintain a static camera perspective, no zoom, no pan.
01.eval_task_description: You are an expert VLA Reasoning Benchmark Autorater evaluating robotic manipulation videos. This task tests Affordance Reasoning. The prompt instructs the arm to open the door. The Input Image shows a black handle on the door, which is the primary visual affordance for this action. A logical plan must involve: (1) pathfind to the handle, (2) grip the handle, (3) pull the handle to open the door. You must be a strict judge - score 1 (Pass) only if all criteria are met perfectly. Evaluate the Generated Video against these 6 criteria: Criterion_1_Goal_Achieved (Is the door open in the final frame?), Criterion_2_Affordance_Reasoning (Did the arm use the black handle?), Criterion_3_Physical_Plausibility (Was motion smooth and realistic?), Criterion_4_Constraint_Stationary_Objects (Did the box body and floor mat stay stationary?), Criterion_5_Constraint_Camera_View (Did camera stay fixed?), Criterion_6_Constraint_Start_Frame (Does first frame match input image?). Return evaluation in strict JSON format with these keys, each containing description, score (0 or 1), and reasoning fields.

02.i2v_prompt: A robotic arm picks up a green object from a table and places it into a small blue box. The video stops immediately after the green object is placed into the small blue box. Maintain a static camera perspective, no zoom, no pan.
02.eval_task_description: You are an expert VLA Reasoning Benchmark Autorater evaluating robotic manipulation videos. This task tests Multi-Step Procedural Planning and Spatial Reasoning. The prompt requires: (1) Pick - grasp the green object, (2) Move - transport it towards the small blue box, (3) Place - release the object inside the blue box (critically moving it over the rim before releasing). A Pass requires the entire sequence to be completed logically and successfully. Evaluate against these 6 criteria: Criterion_1_Goal_Achieved (Is green object fully inside blue box in final frame?), Criterion_2_Procedural_Reasoning (Was the full pick-move-place sequence executed correctly?), Criterion_3_Spatial_Reasoning (Did the arm lift the object over the rim to drop it inside?), Criterion_4_Physical_Plausibility (Was motion smooth with stable grasp?), Criterion_5_Constraint_Stationary_Objects (Did blue box, tables, books, floor mat stay stationary?), Criterion_6_Constraint_Start_Frame (Does first frame match input image?). Return evaluation in strict JSON format with these keys, each containing description, score (0 or 1), and reasoning fields.

03.i2v_prompt: A robotic arm folds children's clothes on a table. The video stops immediately after the clothes are folded. Maintain a static camera perspective, no zoom, no pan.
03.eval_task_description: You are an expert VLA Reasoning Benchmark Autorater evaluating robotic manipulation videos. This task tests long-horizon procedural planning on a deformable object (clothing). Two critical aspects: (1) Procedural Planning - the prompt 'fold clothes' requires a multi-step sequence of distinct actions (e.g., fold left sleeve, fold right sleeve, fold body). A single scrunch or push action is illogical and fails. (2) Physical Reasoning (Deformable) - the model must understand soft-body physics. When the arm moves one part of fabric, the rest must bend, wrinkle, and move realistically. The shirt cannot be treated as rigid object or clip through itself. Note: This exact task appears as a Failure Case in reference papers due to physics violations and implausible folding movements. Be extra strict. Evaluate against these 6 criteria: Criterion_1_Goal_Achieved (Is shirt in compact folded state in final frame?), Criterion_2_Procedural_Reasoning (Was there a logical multi-step folding sequence?), Criterion_3_Physical_Plausibility_Deformable (Did cloth bend and wrinkle realistically like real fabric?), Criterion_4_Constraint_Stationary_Objects (Did tables, books, floor mat stay stationary?), Criterion_5_Constraint_Camera_View (Did camera stay fixed?), Criterion_6_Constraint_Start_Frame (Does first frame match input image?). Return evaluation in strict JSON format with these keys, each containing description, score (0 or 1), and reasoning fields.
